newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: Hyundai plans $1.4 bln UK chip plant.
newsitem.headline: Hyundai plans $1.4 bln UK chip plant.

text.p: Hyundai Electronics Industries Co Ltd, a unit of South Korea's Hyundai Group, said on Tuesday it would invest US$1.4 billion in building a dynamic random access memory (DRAM) chips plant in Dunfermline, Scotland.
Hyundai said the plant was expected to create about 1,000 jobs and would produce 64- and 256-megabit DRAMs on a scale of 30,000 eight-inch wafers per month.
Commercial production was scheduled to start in December 1998, it said in a statement.
"The main purpose of the project is securing a production base in Europe in order to expand our market share in the region and overcome trade barriers," said the statement.

The statement said it had selected Dunfermline, about 15 miles north of Scotland's capital of Edinburgh, because of various conditions Britain offered. billion sterling contract to make semiconducters and electronic goods in Wales.
